newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan parl't cancels 15 pct tax on capital hikes.
newsitem.headline: Jordan parl't cancels 15 pct tax on capital hikes.

text.p: Jordan's parliament has approved cancellation of a 15 percent tax on companies raising their capital bases by transferring money from reserves, officials said on Wednesday.
They said parliament approved the cancellation, part of a wider overhaul of Jordan's companies' law, on Tuesday.

The complete companies' law is not likely to pass parliament until after next week's Moslem Eid holiday, but is not expected to meet any major opposition. It will then be sent for approval to parliament's upper chamber, the Senate.
The decision boosted early trade on Wednesday in two banks planning to boost their capital with transfers from reserves.
Jordan Islamic Bank rose 0.05 dinars to 3.95 dinars and Arab Bank rose 4.50 dinars to 263 dinars at 1053 GMT. Both banks plan bonus shares as part of the transfers.
Brokers welcomed the decision, along with parliamentary approval for scrapping the state's issuing committee which sets prices of new share issues.
"Now firms will be able to determine their own share price without going to the Ministry of Trade and Industry," said Nasser al-Amad, head of United Financial Investments.

Jordanian banks must comply by the end of the year with a Central Bank ruling to increase their capital bases to at least 20 million dinars ($28.2 million). But many have indicated they plan to raise the money through private share placements, which would not have been liable to the 15 percent tax.
